title: EC-guided transfer learning finds SHMT2/MTHFD2 compounds that lower fibroblast collagen
summary: Pre-training a deep feedforward network on the nearest Enzyme Commission family with enough ChEMBL data gave usable drug-target models for SHMT2 (6 known actives) and MTHFD2 (29), where training from scratch failed (MCC 0.00 for SHMT2). Virtual screening of DrugBank gave six candidates; carbimazole, crizotinib and GSK-2018682 reduced TGF-beta-induced collagen production and glycine accumulation in human lung fibroblasts. This is a version 1 preprint abstract; the training sets are very small.
ai_technology: Deep feedforward network pre-trained on EC-hierarchy-selected ChEMBL data and fine-tuned for SHMT2 and MTHFD2 drug-target interaction prediction

evidence.tested: Cell-based assays of three of six screened candidates in TGF-beta-stimulated human lung fibroblasts.
evidence.unknown: Target engagement, specificity and in vivo effect of the repurposed compounds; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts drug-target interactions that drive a DrugBank virtual screen.

source_review.scope: Version 1 abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
